newsitem.title: USA: Texaco in talks to contract Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Texaco in talks to contract Iraqi oil.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Wednesday it was negotiating with the Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) a contract to lift 35,000 to 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi crude.
"We are working on a contract, and we hope to get 35,000-40,000 bpd," said the Texaco official.
Contracts signed between Iraq and U.S. oil companies first must be processed by the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Asset Control (OFAC) to ensure they adhere to U.S. laws.
Treasury was not disclosing details of the list of U.S. companies nor the details of the pending Iraqi oil contracts.
U.N. overseers then must receive the contracts from the Iraqi mission in New York for further review, before potential deals can be approved.
Earlier Wednesday, the United Nations said it still had only received three contracts for approval, one of which was approved.

Turkish state oil company TUPRAS's contract to lift 75,000 bpd was okayed on Tuesday. One of the contract's with the U.N. was believed to be the resubmitted one by Elf Aquitaine, which sources said was rejected initially by the U.N. for technical reasons.

Companies are looking to take part in the $2 billion U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food deal, which allows Iraq to sell oil over a six-month period in order to purchase food and aid for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
